claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can be used to study the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles depends on particle size.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles undergo structural transformations at lower temperatures than larger particles.
The initial material consists of as-prepared FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles with a controlled size distribution extending upward from a few nanometers.
The nanoparticles are initially in their room-temperature phase.
The nanoparticles should be subjected to progressively increasing temperature in an MD or simulated-annealing protocol.
Interatomic potentials adapted to the FeCuCrCoNi composition should be used.
Local compositional fluctuations mediate diffusion and atomic rearrangements during heating.
Surface-to-volume-ratio effects mediate diffusion and atomic rearrangements.
Heating may induce atomic segregation that destabilizes the crystal structure.
Smaller nanoparticles have a higher proportion of surface atoms than larger nanoparticles.
The higher proportion of surface atoms causes smaller nanoparticles to transform or melt at lower temperatures.
MD simulations will show an earlier onset of melting, clustering, or phase change in smaller nanoparticles.
At ambient temperature, the nanoparticles are expected to remain structurally stable.
At ambient temperature, the nanoparticles are expected to retain homogeneous atomic distributions.
The observed trend may depend on the time and temperature ranges accessible to MD.
The observed trend may depend on the selected interatomic potential and simulation parameters.
